rows.slocum: Shallow piston pump (30/50/100/150/200 m, moves seawater) OR deep hydraulic oil/bladder pump (350/1000 m), the modules are easily swappable since the rest of glider has 1000m depth rating
rows.seaglider: 1000m rated oil/bladder pump
rows.note: Slocum modular design gives you flexibility here if you want to use the same glider for both deep and shallow operation.

rows.slocum: Less efficient
rows.seaglider: Very efficient

rows.slocum: Good: the shallow piston pump gives fast inflections.
rows.seaglider: Weak: the main pump is optimised for ~1000 m and has low flow rates for efficient shallow dives
rows.note: Shallow coastal operations favors shallow slocum especially with the optional thruster

rows.seaglider: ~800–860 cc usable
rows.note: Seaglider's budget is tighter when the mission has a large density range. Especially since Seaglider needs some buoyancy to get the antenna out of the water but Slocum has a air bladder at surface to help with this.

rows.slocum: Rudder
rows.seaglider: Roll
rows.note: An advantage of rudder is that it allows tighter turn radius which is especially important for shallow dives, a disadvantage is that although it is a controlled using a magnetically coupled motor housed inside the pressure hull, it still counts as an external moving part and therefore more prone to failure

rows.slocum: Available
rows.seaglider: Not Available
rows.note: ~10 W optional unit. Daily energy rises ~3–5 → ~10–15 Ah/day but transit time roughly halves. Used for thruster-assisted yos, holding horizontal flight at depth, and pushing through the surface lens.

rows.slocum: Yes
rows.seaglider: No
rows.note: It’s a nice help for getting the antenna out of the water but it also introduces another point of failure

rows.slocum: Yes
rows.seaglider: No
rows.note: Nice to have as the last resort if something catastrophic happens but important to remember that glider can not dive again once the weight is dropped and it turns into a simple float until recovered

rows.slocum: Yes
rows.seaglider: No, can be added separately

rows.slocum: Alkaline, 3S lithium primary, 4S lithium primary (standard or extended energy bay), TWR rechargeable Li-ion (standard or extended)
rows.seaglider: Lithium primary only (legacy 24 V + 10 V, or univolt 15 V)

rows.note: Seaglider packs can be purchased directly from Electrochem while Slocum packs need to be purchased from Teledyne

rows.slocum: ~170KHz
rows.seaglider: ~12KHz
rows.note: Seaglider has longer range the advantage in deeper waters, Slocum has higher resolution and best for tighter control within 100m depth, Both can be set to trigger below a certain depth

rows.slocum: Not available
rows.seaglider: You can fly based on a pre-loaded bathymap of the area
rows.note: many advantages such as saving power, being acoustically quiet and a safe backup if there is a problem with altimeter

rows.slocum: Shore cal (recommended), in-situ at-sea cal possible but results may not be reliable
rows.seaglider: In-situ cal easy and accurate, shore cal possible but almost never needed

rows.slocum: Live: Connect directly to GliderDOS at the surface, possible to run scripts on dockserver to automatize communication. Less efficient
rows.seaglider: Indirect: no live terminal. Pilot stages control files (cmdfile, targets, science) that the glider collects at its next call. More efficient
rows.note: By having no direct shell connection, Seagliders save time and data

rows.slocum: SFMC (Teledyne Proprietry), subscription
rows.seaglider: Basestation3 (APL-UW, free, open source, Linux/macOS) or seaglider.pub; you run your own basestation

rows.slocum: Tank ballast + onboard autoballast (centres dive/climb drive automatically)
rows.seaglider: Tank ballast + trim sheet, then manual pitch/VBD/roll trimming from basestation regressions and the Flight Model System
rows.note: Trimming takes much of a Seaglider pilot's early-mission effort. Seaglider provide more options to tune things while Slocum tuning is simpler and more hands-off.

rows.slocum: More complex for new users to troubleshoot especially since the full dive engineering files are extremely large to transmit over iridium
rows.seaglider: Easier to troubleshoot, full dataset is automatically transmitted at the end of each dive

rows.slocum: Possible
rows.seaglider: Not Available

rows.slocum: Usually a small subset of data only on each dive, you can choose to download a larger subset if you want to troubleshoot something specific, the whole dataset is usually too large to be able to download using satellite communication without comms dropping
rows.seaglider: Full dataset is downloaded at each dive

rows.slocum: Iridium (RUDICS primary + dial-up/alternate), Freewave 900 MHz RF modem: for line-of-sight operation and lab work without a cable and for recovery boats, Serial cable for faster data transfer in the lab
rows.seaglider: Iridium (RUDICS primary + dial-up/alternate). Serial cable for Deck/lab comms
rows.note: Slocum iridium costs usually are much higher than Seaglider’s because of the inefficiencies in their file structure and communication methodologies

rows.slocum: Built-in Argos, powered by the emergency circuit, so it keeps transmitting after the main battery fails
rows.seaglider: Optional external tag

rows.slocum: Sensors are integrated by Teledyne, Custom sensor integration possible on G3S with the purchase of Backseat Driver which is a specific version of the Slocum firmware. You can always strap the sensor around the glider. Otherwise it will be a big job.
rows.seaglider: Users have access to all user config files and can easily write their own to integrate complex sensors, Sensor configs can be fixed remotely. There is a large wet payload area with removable hatches for mechanical integration.

rows.slocum: Ships assembled (wings on). Freewave checks on deck, then test dives
rows.seaglider: Seaglider launch needs a laptop and cable on deck plus a satellite link to pilots.

rows.slocum: Optional nose recovery system (line deployed by pilot), strobe make it easier to spot
rows.seaglider: Small-boat cradle or large-vessel lift by the rudder only. Low profile at the surface
